parsed.explanation: The operative regime combines national passport/visa binary screening, federal facility restrictions, and hostile division law. Document mismatch can trigger secondary inspection, refusal, stranding, or fraud-based lifetime ineligibility. Government facilities enforce birth-sex use; refusal risks trespass arrest and misgendered custody. Immigration and corrections custody expose outed trans people to forced programmes, beatings, solitary, and severe abuse. For minors, care bans, name-change denial, and criminalised social transition create guardian investigation and care-denial risks. Litigation and hate-crime statutes give partial recourse, but institutions enforce hostility; no capital outcome documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports/visas show M/F assigned at birth; X marker eliminated; trans-athlete entry ban; discrepancies can trigger secondary screening, denial, confiscation/blocking, stranding, fraud lifetime ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid; court litigation, legal-aid FAQ, some injunctions; no traveller-facing document protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Border document mismatch can escalate into investigation, detention, birth-sex facility placement, or visa adjudication.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration detention reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse; federal corrections impose hormone removal/conversion-style programmes; state trespass arrest led men's-ward hold.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts hear challenges; national hate-crime statute and 2017 bias-murder sentence show some recourse, slow and not traveller-specific.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Discovery at border, facility, or school can move an outed person into custody where birth-sex placement applies.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal/state rules bar birth-mismatched facility use; state law criminalises willful opposite-sex public facility entry after refusal to leave; schools and government buildings affected.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Municipal ordinances and some other-state bans absent; no documented effective relief for visitors against state/federal facility enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Every public-building or school visit can force disclosure, ejection, or trespass arrest.

care_services.exposure: Minor care banned; adolescent clinic closed; religious-provider refusal; HRT continuity and emergency ward placement unclear.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking minors/guardians can be outed, investigated, denied, or separated from treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National and state policies enforce binary sex, remove identity pronoun/name directives, use security language against radical pro-transgender groups; state lacks GI anti-discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law and court rulings persist; 2017 sentence; municipal ordinances.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing may legitimise service denial, refusal to investigate, and profiling at border/facility encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care bans, school dress/name enforcement, teen name-change denial, criminalised social transition; amended certificate lists original sex.
minors_guardians.protection: Court petitions and legal aid exist; same-sex marriage recognition is climate only.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian facilitating care or name use may trigger inquiry, school discipline, or denial.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State lacks GI bias statute/public accommodation; hostile institutional posture may embolden harassment; no recent local bias-killer data after 2017.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law, 2017 sentence, municipal ordinances, survey support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victim response depends on national bias law and local discretion; state recourse weak.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Some orders blocked, but passport rule upheld; adult visitor facility-arrest practice unknown; March 2026 licence exceptions unclear.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation, legal FAQ, ombuds/courts may yield limited relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Enforcement varies by port, shift, state and litigation moment.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less severe than 0.15-A: no capital/execution provision and no documented routine months-long pretrial presentation arrests. It remains below 0.35 because custody, visa fraud, and facility criminalisation create severe possible outcomes.

Similar to 0.25-C in birth-sex custody and facility criminalisation, but the combined national regime adds passport/visa screening, federal correctional abuse, and minor-care restrictions, while some litigation recourse remains.

Much worse than 0.75-C: entry rules are not identity-recognizing, detention can be hostile, facilities are restricted, and care for minors is banned; 0.75-C shows brief detention with reliable release and protection.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime makes an outed adult visitor exposed to denial of entry, document investigation, lifetime ineligibility risk, birth-sex facility enforcement, and severe custody if detained. State law adds criminal trespass and school/public-building exclusion; immigration and federal corrections expose abusive placement and conversion-style programmes. Minors face care denial, name-change barriers, and possible guardian investigation. Courts and hate-crime provisions give partial, slow recourse, but they do not neutralise state and federal institutions actively enforcing hostility. No credible capital evidence places it above the lowest tier, but documented tier-1 exposures justify a high-risk score near the severe boundary.
